sec: Potassium Metabolism · aldosterone in the cortical collecting duct and applied diuretic physiology

items.q: Fill up: Aldosterone's site of action is given as the ______ cell of the collecting tubules, and the paired diagram labels the same cell the ______ cell.
items.exp: The text names the beta-cell of the collecting duct while the figure calls it the principal cell; both refer to the same aldosterone-responsive cell, and the diagram places the type alpha intercalated cell below it. (Book p970)

items.q: Which three functions are listed for aldosterone on this page?
opts: Sodium and water retention, potassium excretion and hydrogen ion excretion
Sodium excretion, potassium retention and hydrogen ion retention
Water retention only, with no effect on potassium
Sodium and water retention, chloride excretion and bicarbonate excretion
items.exp: The three bullets are Na+ and H2O retention, K+ excretion and H+ excretion, which together explain the hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis of mineralocorticoid excess. (Book p970)

items.q: Match the numbered structures in the cortical collecting duct diagram with their identity — 1) Number 2 2) Number 3 3) Number 4 … A) The amiloride-sensitive ENaC channel on the luminal membrane B) The ROMK potassium channel C) The hydrogen exit pathway of the type alpha intercalated cell
items.exp: The figure numbers ENaC as 2 with amiloride drawn blocking it, ROMK as 3, and the apical hydrogen exit of the type alpha intercalated cell as 4, while the basolateral pump carries number 1. (Book p970)

items.q: What sodium to potassium stoichiometry is drawn beside the basolateral pump of the principal cell?
items.exp: The Na+/K+ ATPase in the diagram is annotated 3Na leaving and 2K entering, the classic stoichiometry that sustains the luminal gradient for potassium secretion. (Book p970)

items.q: Assess the diagram's regulatory arrows: I Aldosterone-induced proteins are shown as facilitating the pump, the sodium channel and the potassium channel. II Vasopressin and the AIP arrows converge on hydrogen secretion by the alpha intercalated cell.
items.exp: The facilitatory arrows from AIP run to ENaC, ROMK and the basolateral pump, and the vasopressin arrow reaches the water channel of the principal cell, not hydrogen secretion by the alpha intercalated cell. (Book p970)

items.q: Which of these is NOT one of the classical features listed for Conn's syndrome on this page?
items.exp: The classical triad given for raised aldosterone is hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis; an acidosis would instead suggest a renal tubular acidosis or a mineralocorticoid deficiency state. (Book p970)

items.q: A 38-year-old has blood pressure 168/100 mmHg, potassium 2.8 mEq/L and metabolic alkalosis with suppressed renin. Which row of the page's applied list best accounts for this?
opts: Conn's syndrome, through the aldosterone actions on the principal cell
Liddle's syndrome, through amiloride-sensitive chloride channels
Primary adrenal insufficiency, through loss of aldosterone
Proximal renal tubular acidosis, through bicarbonate wasting
items.exp: The applied aspect names Conn's syndrome as raised aldosterone with the triad of hypertension, hypokalemia and alkalosis, exactly the pattern produced by overactive ENaC, ROMK and the pump in the diagram. (Book p970)

items.q: Assess the diuretic comparison as printed: I Potassium loss is stated to be greater with thiazides than with furosemide. II The printed chain says furosemide blocks the Na+/K+/2Cl- transporter, so luminal electropositivity falls and potassium enters the lumen easily.
items.exp: Statement I is the page's headline. Statement II reverses it: the furosemide chain as printed runs to raised luminal electropositivity, potassium unable to enter the lumen, hypercalciuria and reduced potassium loss, while the thiazide line, which cannot block Na+/K+/2Cl-, is written with a fall in electropositivity and potassium entering easily. Standard tubular physiology puts the lumen-positive potential on the furosemide-sensitive side, so the arrows here are the book's own shorthand rather than the accepted mechanism. (Book p970)

items.q: Fill up: The two small channel sketches contrast a ______ transporter in the furosemide panel, where K+ is drawn trapped inside the cell, against a ______ transporter in the thiazide panel, where K+ ______ the lumen.
items.exp: In the first sketch the Na+/K+/Cl- route is struck through and K+ with its positive charge stays inside the box; in the second the channel is open and the K+ arrow points into the lumen. (Book p970)

items.q: Hypercalciuria appears in the furosemide chain. What consequence does the page attach to it?
items.exp: The arrow reads hypercalciuria leading to reduced K+ loss, which is the page's explanation for why the loop diuretic spares potassium relative to a thiazide. (Book p970)

items.q: All of the following appear as numbered or labelled elements in the collecting duct diagram EXCEPT:
opts: Vasopressin acting on the principal cell
items.exp: The diagram contains ENaC with amiloride, ROMK, AIP, vasopressin, the basolateral pump and the alpha intercalated cell; the Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter belongs to the previous page's thick ascending limb drawing. (Book p970)

items.q: A hyperkalemic hypertensive patient needs a drug that acts on the structure marked as number 2 in this figure. Which agent fits?
items.exp: Number 2 is ENaC, the luminal sodium channel drawn with amiloride blocking it; spironolactone acts on the receptor upstream of AIP rather than on the channel itself. (Book p970)
